results.title: True pricing – guiding consumers within a new pricing paradigm
results.content: Here, we present the results of a large-scale survey experiment with 1400 Dutch and Danish consumers, investigating the effect of the true price presentation format (absolute, relative or no information) on consumers’ choices. For true pricing to support consumers in making more sustainable choices at the point of sale, the information provided must at least be easy and fast to comprehend. Evidence from the existing market trials at Penny or Albert Heijn suggests that when hidden costs are communicated as absolute price premiums, it increases consumers’ focus on the overall true price and the sense that products are generally becoming more expensive (Stein et al., 2024. Journal of Marketing Research, 30(2), 234–245.")), consumers’ price quality schema was measured based on the level of agreement with four items on a 7-point Likert scale after the choice experiment. For consumers to navigate this potentially new pricing paradigm, they need to understand why true prices are higher for some products and how this relates to the product’s level of sustainability.

To help brands navigate this complexity, we have identified six consumer behavior trends that will define 2026, illustrated with real-world examples of how leading brands are responding to evolving customer needs. ***Key Takeaway:** Sustainability has shifted from a differentiator to an expectation, with consumers increasingly holding brands accountable for environmental impact across the full value chain.*. ## What These Consumer Trends Mean for Brands and Market Researchers. Approaches such as ethnographic research, AI-powered analytics and insight communities enable deeper understanding of evolving motivations, unmet needs, and emotional drivers—helping brands design more relevant and resilient strategies that balance data-driven insight with human empathy. Greg is a senior vice president in the Consumer Goods & Retail and Telecommunications industry groups, with additional focus at the intersection of consumer and health, and is in high demand as a speaker and author in the market research and telecom fields.
